fix: Recreate payment intent when order total changes (tip bug)

The payment intent was auto-created with the default 15% tip as soon as
the customer entered contact info. If the customer then changed the tip
(including to 0%), the Stripe amount was never updated — they got charged
the original total with 15% tip baked in.

Now tracks the total used at intent creation and resets the payment state
whenever it diverges (tip change, item edit, delivery fee change, etc.),
causing a fresh intent with the correct amount.

fix: Multi-layer order confirmation to prevent lost orders

Root cause: Safari/iOS aggressively kills pending HTTP requests during
page navigation. In Brian Marciel's case, the payment succeeded but
the /api/payments/confirm call was killed before it reached the server,
resulting in no order being created.

Changes:
1. StripeCheckout.tsx: Use sendBeacon FIRST (synchronous, survives navigation)
   before the fetch call. Increased redirect delay from 500ms to 1200ms.

2. OrderSuccessClient.tsx: Added failsafe that calls /api/payments/confirm
   on the success page. If the order already exists (from sendBeacon/fetch),
   it returns success. If not, it creates the order now.

This provides 3 layers of defense:
- Layer 1: sendBeacon (most reliable during navigation)
- Layer 2: fetch with keepalive (backup)
- Layer 3: Success page retry (final failsafe)
